Model deprecations
See which Claude models are active, deprecated, or retired, and find retirement dates and recommended replacements for models and API parameters.
As safer and more capable models launch, Anthropic regularly retires older ones.
Applications relying on Anthropic models may need occasional updates to keep working.
Impacted customers will always be notified by email and in the documentation.
This page lists all API deprecations, along with recommended replacements.
Overview
Anthropic uses the following terms to describe the model lifecycle:
- Active: The model is fully supported and recommended for use.
- Legacy: The model will no longer receive updates and might be deprecated in the future.
- Deprecated: The model is still functional but no longer recommended.
Anthropic provides a recommended replacement and assigns a retirement date.
- Retired: The model is no longer available for use.
Requests to retired models fail.
The dates on this page apply to Anthropic-operated platforms: the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed), and Microsoft Foundry.
Partner-operated platforms, Amazon Bedrock and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed), set their own retirement schedules, so a model's lifecycle status and dates can differ.
See the Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock (Opus 4.6 and earlier), and Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed) model tables.
Migrating to replacements
Once a model is deprecated, migrate all usage to a suitable replacement before the retirement date.
Requests to models past the retirement date will fail.
To help measure the performance of replacement models on your tasks, consider thorough testing of your applications with the new models well before the retirement date.
For specific instructions on migrating to the latest Claude models, see Migration guides.
Notifications
Anthropic notifies customers with active deployments for models with upcoming retirements, providing at least 60 days' notice before model retirement for publicly released models.
Auditing model usage
To help identify usage of deprecated models, you can access an audit of your API usage.
Follow these steps:
- Go to the Usage page in Claude Console.
- Click Export.
- Review the downloaded CSV to see usage broken down by API key and model.
This audit helps you locate any instances where your application is still using deprecated models, allowing you to prioritize updates to newer models before the retirement date.
Best practices
- Regularly check the documentation for updates on model deprecations.
- Test your applications with newer models well before the retirement date of your current model.
- Update your code to use the recommended replacement model as soon as possible.
- Contact the support team if you need help with migration or have any questions.
Deprecation downsides and mitigations
Anthropic currently deprecates and retires models to ensure capacity for new model releases.
This comes with downsides:
- Users who value specific models must migrate to new versions.
- Researchers lose access to models for ongoing and comparative studies.
- Model retirement introduces safety- and model welfare-related risks.
At some point, Anthropic hopes to make past models publicly available again.
In the meantime, Anthropic has committed to long-term preservation of model weights and other measures to help mitigate these impacts.
For more details, see Commitments on Model Deprecation and Preservation.

Commitments of Traders (COT) Reports Descriptions
- Introduction and Classification Methodology
- The Commodity Futures Trading Commission (Commission or CFTC) publishes the Commitments of Traders (COT) reports to help the public understand market dynamics.
Specifically, the COT reports provide a breakdown of each Tuesday’s open interest for futures and options on futures markets in which 20 or more traders hold positions equal to or above the reporting levels established by the CFTC.
The CFTC releases the weekly COT reports in static format to support the historical usage patterns of industry professionals viewing and accessing each week’s data.

It is possible that there’s a lack of a sufficient number of Large Traders with respect to the contract market in question.

Externó que es importante reflexionar sobre las

económica en ese país.
Opinó que es adecuado
comunicar que, en virtud de que las condiciones
macroeconómicas en México difieren de las de
Estados Unidos, nuestras decisiones no tendrían por
qué reaccionar de manera mecánica ante ajustes a
la tasa de fondos federales.
Estimó que, dada la
evolución reciente de la inflación, y en la medida en

proceso desinflacionario, en las siguientes

en la tasa de referencia.

como en toda ocasión el Banco de México mantiene
un monitoreo constante de la postura absoluta y
relativa para garantizar que siga favoreciendo la
convergencia de la inflación a la meta.
Otro miembro destacó que, a casi siete meses del
inicio del conflicto en Medio Oriente, los retos para la
economía mundial persisten y el panorama
económico continúa caracterizado por una alta
incertidumbre.
Indicó que los precios del petróleo y
sus derivados siguen el evados en un contexto en
que distintos amortiguadores, como las reservas
estratégicas de energéticos, se han reducido.

que a ello se suma la proximidad del invierno en el
hemisferio norte y el crecimiento de los centros de
datos ligados a la inteligencia artificial , asociados
con alta demanda energética.
Sostuvo que ante este
escenario se requiere cautela en las decisiones de
política monetaria.
Resaltó que en México el impacto
del actual choque global en energéticos sobre la
inflación ha sido menor que el observado durante el
episodio de 2022.

recientemente representantes de empresas

obstáculo para el crecimiento el a

tre el diferencial y el tipo de cambio.

año.
Subrayó que, en estas condiciones, aumentos
en tasas externas no necesariamente requerirán una
respuesta automática en la política monetaria de
México.
Argumentó que ello dependerá de cómo
incidan en el panorama inflacionario doméstico.
Subrayó que el reto en el último año ha sido adoptar
gradualmente una postura congruente con el
panorama inflacionario afectado por ajustes de
precios relativos y no por presiones de demanda, al
tiempo que ha habido una disminución gradual del
grado de restricción monetaria.
Notó que, dadas las
condiciones macroeconómicas, la postura
continuará siendo restrictiva.
No obstante, advirtió
que no incorporar estas condiciones en las
decisiones de política podría implicar un grado de
restricción mayor al requerido.
Así, consideró que
existen elementos para discutir la conveniencia de
realizar un ajuste fino a la baja de la tasa de
referencia.
Precisó que esto no representa una
decisión anticipada, sino una discusión que se debe
mantener abierta.
Agregó que su eventual
materialización d ependerá de que continúe la
tendencia a la baja de la inflación y de que las
condiciones financieras permanezcan ordenadas.
Aseveró que la postura continuará siendo
congruente con el entorno macroeconómico, la
trayectoria prevista para la inflación y el an claje de
sus expectativas.

La Junta de Gobierno evaluó el panorama
inflacionario.
Valoró el comportamiento del tipo de
cambio, que las economías de México y Estados
Unidos atraviesan por etapas distintas del ciclo
económico, la ausencia de presiones de demanda
en México y el grado d e restricción monetaria
implementado.
Así, con la presencia de todos sus
miembros, decidió por unanimidad mantener el
objetivo para la Tasa de Interés Interbancaria a un
día en 6.50%.

desinflacionario y el comportamiento esperado de
sus determinantes, incluyendo el traspaso del tipo de
cambio a los precios del consumidor, las condiciones

las condiciones macroeconómicas en México son
distintas a las de Estados Unidos, la política
monetaria no tendría que reaccionar de manera
mecánica ante los ajustes previstos a la tasa de
fondos federales .
El Banco Central reafirma su
compromiso con su mandato prioritario y la
necesidad de perseverar en sus esfuerzos por

Everything about Fable 5.5 in this piece is a claim from one X account, unverified, and labelled as such throughout.

The signal is a single paragraph written the way people write when they are excited, which makes it worth taking apart clause by clause.
The useful split is not important-versus-unimportant.
It is checkable-versus-not.

A checkpoint is a saved state of a model's weights at a point during or after a training run.
A single run produces many of them, at intervals, for reasons that include resuming after a crash, comparing intermediate quality, and picking the version to post-train.
Two checkpoints of the same run are the same model at two moments.
They can differ noticeably on some tasks and not at all on others, and neither difference is promised to you in a document.
Which is why “better than first” is the emptiest phrase in the post.
Better at what, measured how, by whom, against what?
There is no eval, no comparison prompt, no side-by-side, and no third party who has touched either build.
The poster is comparing their own impressions of two things nobody else has seen.
That may be an honest report.

- U.S.
spot Bitcoin ETFs posted net outflows of $228.6 million this week, after losing $681.1 million the week before.

Bitcoin ETF investors spent another week heading for the exits.
U.S.
spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $82.4 million on Friday, according to Decrypt’s ETF tracker, capping a week in which outflows outweighed inflows on three of five trading days.
The funds lost a net $228.6 million for the week, according to SoSoValue, following a $681.1 million drain the week before.
Over the two weeks, about $910 million has left the funds.
It was a choppy stretch.
A $175.7 million inflow on Tuesday was wiped out a day later by $261.4 million in redemptions, the week’s worst session.
Thursday brought a modest $5.1 million inflow before selling resumed Friday.
Wednesday’s selling coincided with a hot inflation print.
The consumer price index showed prices up 3.7% year over year in September, above the 3.6% forecast.
A hotter-than-expected producer price reading followed Thursday, reviving bets on another Federal Reserve interest rate hike.
Bitcoin briefly slipped below $80,000 on Thursday, and nearly $950 million in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated over 24 hours, about 90% of them bullish longs, according to CoinGlass.
The drop also pushed Bitcoin below the average ETF holder’s estimated cost basis near $82,300, Nexo analyst Iliya Kalchev told Decrypt.
When inflation runs hot, the Fed tends to keep raising rates, pushing up Treasury yields and making a nearly risk-free return of around 5% a tough competitor for riskier bets like Bitcoin.
Higher rates also make borrowing costlier and lift the dollar, squeezing the cheap credit that leveraged crypto traders depend on.
The back-to-back red weeks have dragged October deep into negative territory.
After opening the month with roughly $293 million in inflows, the funds are now down about $615 million for October, based on Decrypt’s tracker.
The slide began in earnest on Oct.
7, when a $484.9 million exit marked the funds’ worst day since June.
Ethereum and Solana ETFs have also been in the red this month.
Spot Bitcoin ETFs are exchange-traded funds that hold actual Bitcoin.
They trade on stock exchanges like ordinary shares, giving investors exposure through a regular brokerage account without buying or storing the asset themselves.
Since launching in January 2024, they’ve drawn $57.3 billion in cumulative net inflows, according to Decrypt’s tracker, making them a fixture of Wall Street’s crypto exposure.
Because issuers report flows daily, and institutions and financial advisers account for much of the money, the figures have become a closely watched gauge of investor sentiment.
Total net assets stand at $104.29 billion, according to SoSoValue, while Decrypt’s tracker puts the figure at $100.2 billion.
Bitcoin closed Friday near $81,590, down from about $82,337 a week earlier.

In the race for U.S.
Senate in Texas, Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton are competitive with only two points separating the two candidates among likely voters statewide.
Talarico is +4 points against Paxton among registered voters, notched down slightly from six points last month.
Looking at the generic congressional ballot question, the Republicans are +5 points against the Democrats on the ballot among likely voters.
However, the margin narrows among registered voters where Republicans are +3 points.
Less than one month ago, the Democratic candidates had a 3-pont edge among registered voters.
In the Texas governor’s race, incumbent Republican Greg Abbott is +4 points against Democratic challenger Gina Hinojosa among likely voters.
Among registered voters, just one point separates the two gubernatorial candidates.
Previously, Hinojosa had a 3-point edge against Abbott among registered voters.
Sharp partisan divides underscore these hotly contested races as do impressions of President Donald Trump and financial worries.
- Two points separate Talarico (47%) and Paxton (45%) among likely voters in the U.S.
Senate race in Texas.
Among independents who say they are likely to vote, a majority (52%) support Talarico.
A majority (53%) of likely voters statewide think, regardless of whom they support, Paxton will win the Senate seat.
- 51% of likely voters report they are more inclined to support the Republican running for Congress in their district than the Democrat (46%) on the ballot.
60% of likely voters say they also think the Republican congressional candidate will actually win.
- Nearly four in ten likely voters statewide (38%) say their congressional vote is mainly a vote against President Trump while 27% say their ballot is mostly a vote for the president.
34% say President Trump does not matter much to their vote.
Of those who say President Trump has little bearing on their vote, a majority approves of his job performance.
- In the Texas governor's race, Abbott (49%) edges Hinojosa (45%) among likely voters statewide, and seven in ten likely voters in Texas (70%) report they think Abbott will win.
- President Trump's approval rating in Texas is upside down (46% approve to 54% disapprove) among likely voters.
- 43% of likely voters say their family finances have gotten worse in the last year.
18% say they have gotten better, and 43% report there has been little change to their financial picture during the last year.
Democrats (58%) are more likely than Republicans (19%) to say their personal finances have declined.
